text: The Lesson 7 runbook covers detection through communication only in the abstract. The firewall-rule incident just lived through all of it for real -- exactly what turns a runbook from theory into something trusted.
Mara writes a worked example in the runbook's own structure: detection, triage, root cause, remediation, validation -- short enough for a future on-call responder to use fast.
A worked example alone only helps if the next thing looks like this exact incident. What prevents the next version of the mistake is a new standing control.
Two parts: a per-change gate requiring documented justification and a second reviewer on every firewall rule change, plus a periodic audit of existing rule scopes.
The gate alone wouldn't have caught this rule -- it predates the gate. The periodic review alone is too slow to stop a new mistake. Together, they cover both directions.
